column1: # The explained list of the CodeBrix.Android parity score (tools/CodeBrix.Android.ParityScore).
# A public DependencyProperty that no native handler maps is "declined" unless a line below explains it: Core itself,
# the policy layer or the platform answers for it, so a handler has nothing to map. Every line is a written policy
# decision; add one only when the reason is true of the code today, and remove it when a handler starts mapping the
# property (the report then counts it as mapped anyway).
#   declaring type (full name, or * for any type) | property member name | category | reason (one sentence)
#   core-layout   Core measures and arranges every element; the native views replay Core's slots.
#   core-tree     Object-model state Core keeps (names, data context, resources, styles); nothing native shows it.
#   core-input    Core's input regime owns hit testing, focus navigation, drag and manipulation; native views forward input.
#   core-template Core applies templates and visual states; a native handler does not use them (AP6 C6, CBAND0001).
#   policy        The policy layer answers for it (theme bridge, size classes, type scale, motion).
#   platform      The Android platform supplies the behaviour (system focus visuals, IME, accessibility).
